name: Iran
summary_text: Iran is one of the world's most severe environments for trans people — but with a unique bifurcation. Same-sex conduct carries the death penalty, and a trans woman was raped in Ministry of Intelligence custody (the documented case of Ghazal Marzban in Evin Prison, 2023). The Tehran City Council ordered trans people to avoid "busy" areas of the capital. Trans people who have not had surgery face immorality and indecency provisions (imprisonment, fines, lashes) and documented forced-transition pressure — 6Rang describes "40 years of forcing gay people to choose between transitioning and death." However, transsexuality IS legally recognised in Iran (under a 1987 fatwa by Ayatollah Khomeini), and gender-affirming surgery is state-funded — making Iran one of the few countries in the region with any legal recognition of trans identity, and a trans medical-tourism hub. A post-operative trans visitor with matching documents is in a structurally different and better position than a pre-operative or non-binary visitor, or anyone perceived as same-sex-active — who face the death penalty, state-custody sexual violence, and forced-transition coercion.

sources.title: Tehran Tells Transgender People To Avoid 'Busy' Areas, Highlighting Difficulties Faced By LGBT Community
sources.claim_summary: RFE/RL (March 2024): Tehran's city council spokesman said transgender people should congregate only in certain parts of the capital and avoid 'busy' areas - official guidance highlighting how the LGBT community is shunned; most LGBT Iranians hide their orientation and lead double lives for fear of persecution.

sources.title: Letter from Prison: Ghazal Marzban Recounts Rape at a Ministry of Intelligence Detention Facility - Hrana
sources.claim_summary: HRANA (Aug 2026): trans woman Ghazal Marzban, incarcerated in Evin Prison, recounts in a letter that after her May 2023 arrest she was taken blindfolded to a Ministry of Intelligence detention facility, searched, and raped by a masked man; officials promised release in exchange for silence and threatened her against speaking out.

6Rang submission (Feb 2025) to the UN Independent Expert on SOGI, 'They See Us as Criminals: The Forces Driving LGBTIQ+ Displacement from Iran': survey of 25 LGBTIQ+ people who fled Iran (96% from ethnic minorities) documenting systematic persecution driving displacement.

sources.title: Iran | Outright International
sources.claim_summary: Outright International country overview (updated March 2026): same-sex relations criminalised with a maximum penalty of death; trans people who have undergone surgery may change legal gender markers but face violence, discrimination and harassment; strict censorship bans LGBTIQ media; the UN Fact-Finding Mission (March 2025) found discriminatory public statements by officials at the highest levels and that LGBTQ+ people arrested in the 2022 protests suffered 'dehumanising insults, threats and treatment amounting to torture'.

UK Home Office CPIN Iran: Sexual orientation and gender identity and expression (v5.0, Dec 2025): the Islamic Penal Code criminalises all same-sex activity (flogging to death penalty); no discrimination protections; convictions on pretext of more severe charges; gender reassignment surgery is permitted and may be subsidised after a 'gender identity disorder' diagnosis, but is invasive and often sub-standard; recognition only after surgery, sterilisation and a lengthy legal process; an LGBT+ person living openly without recognised surgery is likely to face persecution.

sources.title: Trans medical tourism is booming in Iran, while transitions are forced on locals - LGBTQ Nation
sources.claim_summary: LGBTQ Nation (Oct 2025): trans medical tourism is booming in Iran - the government promotes discounted gender-affirming surgery packages to foreigners for currency, while the industry's expertise stems from decades of forcing gay people to choose between transitioning and death; also reports 100 trans inmates presumed dead after an Israeli attack on an Iranian prison.

sources.title: Iran Pays for Gender-Transition Surgery, but It Comes at a Cost — Your Dignity - Business Insider
sources.claim_summary: Business Insider (July 2024): Iran's transgender policy might seem surprisingly liberal - the state pays for gender-transition surgery - but 'it comes at a cost: your dignity'; profiles Shayan Varamini and examines the paradox of state-funded transition alongside criminalisation of homosexuality.

6Rang submission to Iran's UPR (48th session, Jan-Feb 2025): human-rights violations against lesbian, gay, bisexual and transgender people in Iran - documentation of persecution, violence and legal discrimination.

sources.title: Iran: Two More Executions for Homosexual Conduct | Human Rights Watch
sources.claim_summary: HRW (Nov 2005): 'Iran: Two More Executions for Homosexual Conduct' - documents executions for consensual same-sex conduct under Iran's penal code, part of the pattern of death-penalty application to LGBT people.
